summary.title: Zalando RESTful API and Event Guidelines
summary.one_liner: Zalando's internal-turned-public rulebook for designing RESTful JSON APIs and event types, covering naming, HTTP methods and status codes, headers, versioning, deprecation and event design.
takeaways: Design APIs OpenAPI-first: write the specification before implementation and get peer review early.
Follow concrete naming rules: pluralized resource names, kebab-case path segments, snake_case query parameters and properties, verb-free URLs.
Use HTTP methods and status codes precisely, return problem JSON, never expose stack traces, and use 429 with headers for rate limits.
Avoid breaking changes: use media type versioning rather than URL versioning, mark deprecations with Deprecation and Sunset headers, and get client consent before shutdown.
Events are part of the service interface: define event types with ownership, semantic versioning, unique IDs, and robust duplicate handling.
summary.summary: This is Zalando's public RESTful API and event guideline document, organized as a numbered list of rules labeled MUST, SHOULD, or MAY per RFC 2119. The page covers the rationale (API First, API as a Product, Postel's law), then detailed rules for REST basics such as data formats, URLs, JSON payloads, HTTP methods, status codes and headers, plus hypermedia, compatibility, deprecation, and event categories and design. The excerpt shown ends partway through the meta information section on OpenAPI info fields and semantic versioning, so the later sections were not visible in the text provided. The guidance is prescriptive reference material rather than a step-by-step tutorial.
